title: Segmented iterators 重訪——讓編譯器看見 deque 的分段結構，把通用演算法的 SIMD 加速找回來
summary: std::deque 天生分段：一排 T** block 索引指向若干段連續的 T*。但標準演算法把它當扁平 range 走，每個 ++it 都隱含一個 block 邊界檢查，這個資料相依分支擋住 auto-vectorization——Austern 2000 年量到約 20% 吞吐損失。解法是 Austern 的 segmented iterator：把迭代器拆成不可解參考的 segment iterator（T**）與可解參考的 local iterator（T*），用 hierarchical_fill 把 range 切成頭段＋整段內部＋尾段，讓中間每個 std::fill 拿到純連續 range、暴露可向量化的 tight 內迴圈。boostedcpp.net 2026-05 評測：幾何平均加速 5.9×（MSVC 2026 小型別），fill corner case 衝到 17.16×。跨編譯器分歧極大：MSVC 對 SIMD store 最積極且忽略 unroll pragma，GCC 16 需要 #pragma unroll(4) 才從 1.96× 翻身到 3.13×，Clang 加 unroll hint 反而退步。元素變大（32-byte MyFatInt）時加速收斂到 2.4–3.3×，瓶頸從邊界檢查轉為記憶體頻寬。這是 Stepanov zero-overhead 抽象命題的一次體檢：零開銷不靠抽象越薄，而靠抽象暴露的資訊剛好夠編譯器做對的優化。
widget_questions: What is the actual shape of the segmentation-awareness payoff across five compiler configurations (MSVC 2026, Clang, Clang+unroll, GCC 16, GCC+unroll) for 4-byte MyInt vs 32-byte MyFatInt — and how far does the geomean diverge from the fill-only corner case?

Which iterator owns which traversal level — the non-dereferenceable T** segment iterator that walks the deque's block map, versus the dereferenceable T* local iterator that walks the contiguous elements inside one block?
As the deque block size shrinks from 512 down to 2 elements, how does the fraction of elements stuck in vectorizable interior tight-loop code erode as boundary-transition density rises?

How does the same fill operation decompose across three views — the naive flat std::fill that hides a per-increment boundary branch, the segmented_iterator_traits vocabulary, and the complete hierarchical_fill that splits the range into partial-initial + full-interior + partial-final segments?

For the same hierarchical_fill rewrite, how do the three compilers diverge — MSVC's aggressive SIMD-store recognition that ignores unroll pragmas, GCC's conservative default that needs an explicit hint to reach parity, and Clang's regression when an explicit unroll hint is added?
